The life history of Stinging catfish (Heteropneustes fossilis) begins with the release of demersal, adhesive eggs measuring between 1.3 and 1.5 mm in diameter. From these egg dimensions, the wet weight at birth has been calculated at 0.0012 grams [Wwb = 0.0012 grams], reflecting the small, yolk-dependent progeny typical of many siluriform fishes. Embryonic development proceeds rapidly at a temperature of 29 °C [T = 29 °C], with the chorion rupture and larval eclosion occurring after just 4 days [ab = 4 days]. This brief incubation period is characteristic of tropical freshwater teleosts, where elevated thermal regimes accelerate ontogenetic processes, enabling the prolarvae to transition quickly from the yolk-sac stage to active exogenous feeding.

As juvenile Heteropneustes fossilis grow, a distinct milestone is achieved when individuals reach a total length at puberty of 12 centimeters [Lp = 12 centimeters], at which point the corresponding wet weight at puberty is approximately 9.3 grams [Wwp = approximately 9.3 grams]. This size threshold indicates the onset of reproductive capacity, a stage associated with significant morphological changes that align with patterns observed in other siluriform fishes inhabiting tropical floodplain systems. The transition from immature post-metamorphic juvenile to a sexually mature individual involves considerable mass accumulation, with the ultimate wet weight of fully grown adults recorded at 420 grams [Wwi = 420 grams] and an ultimate total length of 41.2 centimeters [Li = 41.2 centimeters]. These asymptotic body dimensions are among the largest documented for the species, indicating a substantial scope for somatic growth throughout the lifespan.

Reproductive output in Heteropneustes fossilis has been quantified under controlled laboratory conditions. At a stable water temperature of 25 °C [T = 25 °C], gravid females are capable of producing approximately 43 eggs per day [Ri = approximately 43 eggs per day], a rate inferred from total annual fecundity estimates. This high daily reproductive output positions the species among the more fecund members of the Heteropneustidae, with a capacity for sustained batch spawning over extended breeding seasons. The maximum recorded longevity for the species at this same thermal condition (25 °C [T = 25 °C]) is approximately 2372 days [am = approximately 2372 days], a lifespan that facilitates multiple reproductive cycles and underscores an iteroparous life-history strategy adapted to stable, warm freshwater habitats.

Maturation and the onset of first breeding are linked to size rather than strictly to age. The total length at which reproductive activity initiates has been established at 12 centimeters [Lp = 12 centimeters], with corresponding body mass at puberty of 9.3 grams [Wwp = 9.3 grams]. These values are derived from length-weight regressions calibrated for the species, where the relationship follows a power equation (0.0043 * L^3.09). The data indicate that individuals channel resources toward somatic growth until this size threshold, after which gonadal maturation and spawning effort commence. The ultimate adult size, with an asymptotic wet weight of 420 grams [Wwi = 420 grams] and a total length of 41.2 centimeters [Li = 41.2 centimeters], is reached gradually over several seasons, as confirmed by growth monitoring of captive populations maintained at 25 °C.

Under optimal rearing conditions at 29 °C [T = 29 °C], the age at which Heteropneustes fossilis completes yolk-sac absorption and achieves free-swimming status is just 4 days [ab = 4 days]. This extraordinarily rapid embryonic phase is followed by an extended period of somatic development, with senescence ultimately occurring after a lifespan of approximately 2372 days [am = approximately 2372 days] when maint at a temperature of 25 °C [T = 25 °C]ained at 25 °C. The asymptotic total length of 41.2 centimeters [Li = 41.2 centimeters] exceeds the typical range for related siluriforms, a likely consequence of the species' predatory niche in productive freshwater systems. The wet weight at birth of 0.0012 grams [Wwb = 0.0012 grams] is a direct consequence of the small egg diameter, which in turn influences larval survival through the critical period of first exogenous feeding onset.
